summary.headline: PG Electroplast Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.2% YoY to INR2,034 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% amid commodity and rupee pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue crossed INR2,000 crore for the first time, up 35.2% YoY, with EBITDA up 12.1% to INR156.2 crore and net profit up 12.9% to INR75.3 crore. Growth came from double-digit volume growth plus a similar ASP increase as copper, aluminium and resin costs and rupee depreciation were partly passed through. Gross margin percentage softened QoQ and YoY, which management attributed to pass-through mechanics rather than per-unit erosion. The company reports a net cash position, and the compressor, refrigerator and washing machine capacity build-out is the main medium-term theme.

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,401 crore, up 38.1% YoY; volume up about 20-22% and ASP up about 10-12% YoY. Management guided roughly 20% plus volume growth for the full year.

segments.name: Washing machine
segments.commentary: Revenue INR211 crore, up 67.2% YoY; fully automatic machines grew about 150% YoY. Resin cost pass-through lagged in the quarter, with management calling the margin impact much larger than 20-30 bps.

segments.name: Coolers
segments.commentary: Revenue almost INR19 crore, up 3.4% YoY.

segments.name: Electronics (EMS)
segments.commentary: 5.3% of revenue, up 65.3% YoY; largely job work with stable margins per management.

segments.name: Plastic moulding and components
segments.commentary: Revenue INR294.6 crore, up 7% YoY; job-work style model where customers specify resin sourcing, so limited margin impact.

segments.name: Goodworth Electronics (JV)
segments.commentary: Sales INR177.3 crore vs INR147.5 crore last year; EBITDA INR6.3 crore vs INR4.3 crore.

segments.name: PG Technoplast (wholly-owned subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Reported sales of about INR1,600 crore for the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Operating margin aspiration of about 8% for full FY27; management stated this is not guidance and the Q1 operating margin was about 7.3%.
Management expects FY27 earnings to surpass FY25 levels if second-half sales are good.
Full-year volume growth of about 20%+ expected in base case, with 4-5% upside versus industry growth if the compressor plant ramps.
Price increases of roughly 10-15% expected for brands post GST cut, with the next pass-through targeted for the December quarter.
Management expects 25-30% growth in FY27-FY28 and sees no growth challenge for the next 2-3 years; FY29 may be a consolidation year.
AC share of sales expected to fall from 60-65% to 50-55% over 2-3 years.
Management declined to give revenue guidance, quarterly guidance, or FY27 capex detail beyond INR400 crore for the year.
capex_capacity: Washing machine plant in DMIC Greater Noida is online with 1.8 million units annual capacity; total washing machine capacity to reach about 3 million. Target utilisation of 70-80% by FY28.

Refrigerator plant at Sri City (1.2 million units) targeted for commercial production in Q4 FY27; anchor customer tied up with about 30-35% capacity commitment. Phase 1 covers direct-cool and side-by-side models; frost-free and multi-door follow in phase 2.

Compressor plant at Supa: first 2 million-unit line on track for mass production in December-January; commissioning took about 6 months. Second line planned for April-May 2027 decision, with about 3-4 months lead time; the land and building can accommodate 4 lines.
Compressor economics: one line at 80% utilisation is about 1.6-1.7 million units at about INR2,850-2,900 per unit; Indian compressor prices cited at INR2,800-3,000.
FY27 capex about INR400 crore, mainly completing compressor and refrigerator projects, plus a new land parcel at Salarpur to consolidate plastic moulding operations from Greater Noida.
PG Technoplast Rajasthan facility is coming online. Management targets fixed asset turn above 4x.
demand_pricing: Industry RAC primary sales grew about 15% YoY in Q1; with ASP growth of 10-12%, primary value growth was about 20-25%. Secondary sales were reportedly better than primary, with channel and brand inventory near normal (estimated 4.5-5.5 million units).
Management expects RAC outsourcing share to keep rising; brands are using outsourcing to protect margins amid high competition.
Price hikes in July-September have had limited success; some brands took and rolled back increases.

Compressor imports: about 50-60% of India's requirement still imported. Imports capped at 25% of FY25 volumes (about 2.5 million units) until 31 March 2027, then no imports. Management sees possible tightening from January-February 2027.
Copper above $14,000/tonne versus $7,000-8,000 earlier; rupee around INR95.5-96/USD. Management said commodity pass-through remains incomplete.
Imports of inner grooved copper tubing (IGT) to be restricted from November.

qa_highlights.question: What was the RAC volume and ASP split, and how much of the commodity cost increase has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: RAC volume grew about 20-22% and ASP about 10-12%. Management said pass-through was partial, varied by customer, and a further price increase is expected from the December quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company near normal margins, and can it return to 10% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to a 10% margin, saying the business is per-piece priced. It expects per-piece margins to normalise and operating margins ex-PLI to improve significantly, with a reported margin slightly above last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much is compressor capex and what margin will compressors add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex split by segment would be shared offline, and total FY27 capex is about INR400 crore. Compressors are expected to be margin-additive as the first line mainly serves in-house AC needs.

qa_highlights.question: What was washing machine utilisation before the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier capacity ran at about 70% annualised utilisation, with peak months above 100%. Target is 70-80% on the expanded capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of rising inventory values and the working capital build?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5 lakh AC inventory is now about INR940 crore versus about INR700 crore last year, reflecting commodity inflation and strategic stocking of compressors and IGT. Inventory was about INR100 crore lower than planned due to June softness.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not share order book numbers. The AC season order book is not yet rebuilt and will start building in September-October for the December season; washing machine volume commitments exist but are not disclosed.

financial_highlights.change: Net cash company; modest debt at end-Q1
